Its behavior depends entirely on a helper not shown here

terms.meaning: a check that stops the program with an error when a condition is false

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Renewables delay check
sections.what: Confirms that renewables projects have no delay values and exits with success or failure. It changes nothing.
sections.why: The header says no delay values exist, so this keeps a recorded audit without writing anything.
sections.watch_out: A pass only means the helper found no delay values; the helper itself should be checked before relying on that result.

summary: A check-only script that confirms renewables projects have no delay values, so no approximate-date flags are needed.
purpose: Keep a recorded audit that the renewables group has been checked and has nothing to flag.
why: The header says no delay values currently exist, so the script deliberately makes no derived values and no database writes.
how: The script calls the shared check assertNoDelayValues with the renewables group name. If the check passes it exits with success. If it throws, it prints the error and exits with a failure code.
inputs: The renewables group name, read from the database through the helper.
outputs: No database writes and no derived values. Only an exit status and any error message.
risks: If renewables projects later get delay values, the check will fail, which is the intended warning and means someone must review them.
debug: If the script fails, find the renewables project that now has a delay value. Then check the helper file to confirm what the check reads.
